key_insight: A large-deformation viscoelastic model captures open-cell foam’s rate-sensitive response and volumetric–distortional coupling, with validation predictions largely within experimental uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: The model supports finite-element prediction of foam deformation for cushioning and impact-protection design.
method: Combine equilibrium hyperelasticity with multiple nonlinear Maxwell-like contributions.
Use logarithmic-strain invariants to represent large deformations and volumetric–distortional coupling.
Calibrate with compression, tension, and lateral-strain data across decadal strain rates; screen for compaction bands.
evidence_signal: Finite-element predictions were tested against intentionally inhomogeneous experiments spanning strain rates and deformation types, with agreement largely within experimental uncertainty bounds.
watch_item: Compaction-band formation can invalidate the homogeneous-deformation assumptions used for calibration and requires explicit screening.
paper_title: Large-deformation constitutive modeling of viscoelastic foams: Application to an open-cell foam material
